paper_metadata.title: Quantum-inspired variational algorithms for partial differential equations: Application to financial derivative pricing

experiments.description: Variational quantum Monte Carlo / neural-network quantum state solver applied to the d-dimensional diffusion (heat) equation with Gaussian initial conditions, evaluated across multiple dimensions and qubit counts against forward Euler.

algorithm.variant: Autoregressive neural-network quantum state with McLachlan variational principle
algorithm.optimizer: Adam for pre-training; linear solve with SVD-regularized update for evolution
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Pre-training for 50k iterations; evolution run for 20k iterations; fixed time step δt = 5e-5

hyperparameters.learning_rate_schedule: warm-start for first 1/10 of training, then decayed by factor 10 at 3/7 and 5/7 of total training iterations

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initialized by pre-training to match the initial condition using stochastic gradient descent

optimizer_settings.learning_rate_schedule: warm-start then step decays at 3/7 and 5/7 of total training iterations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The PDE state is discretized on a regular grid with 2^n grid points and represented as an n-qubit computational basis state; each mesh point maps to one basis state.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize the Euclidean distance between the time-evolved PDE state and the variational trial state under McLachlan’s variational principle.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Dirichlet boundary conditions implemented via a source function; periodic boundary conditions tested directly on the mesh.

problem_instance.description: d-dimensional heat equation with either periodic or Dirichlet boundary conditions and discrete isotropic Gaussian initial condition.

dataset_specification.description: Initial condition u0(x) = ∏_i e^{-t} I_{x_i}(t), where I_x is the modified Bessel function; dimensions tested include d = 1,2,3,4 and qubit-per-dimension settings n/d = 4 or 5.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Spatial domain discretized on a regular hypercube mesh; no external dataset used.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Average relative error versus forward Euler over 20k iterations; running time measured over 2k iterations; results averaged over 5 random seeds.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: Varies with problem size; reported settings include n = d × (n/d) with n/d ∈ {4,5} and d up to 4 in error tables, and up to n = 16 qubits in runtime comparison.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Finite-difference discretization of the Laplacian using central differences; mesh encoding of the PDE state.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Relative error computed from space-time history of the variational state versus Euler solution.

speedup_claims.factor: O(T × 2^(2n)) for forward Euler vs O(TB poly(n)) for the proposed method
speedup_claims.conditions: as stated in the paper for a grid of size |bΩ| = 2^n
speedup_claims.caveats: The proposed method is approximate and has overhead from sampling, forward/backward passes, and matrix-element extraction.

speedup_claims.factor: faster than forward Euler at n = 16 qubits
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper states this crossover explicitly; exact wall-clock values depend on problem size and batch size.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(TB poly(n)); forward pass O(TBn^2), sampling O(TBn^3)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(T × 2^(2n)) for forward Euler as stated in the paper
complexity_analysis.crossover_n: Paper states the method is already faster than forward Euler for n = 16 qubits

experiments.description: Ablation study on batch size for the same diffusion-equation VMC solver, measuring runtime and relative error as batch size increases.

algorithm.variant: Autoregressive neural-network quantum state with Monte Carlo batch-size ablation
algorithm.optimizer: Adam for pre-training; SVD-regularized linear update for evolution
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Fixed evolution protocol; batch size varied to study performance
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Same pre-trained initialization as the diffusion experiment

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same mesh-to-qubit encoding as the diffusion experiment; batch size changes only the Monte Carlo estimation of M and V.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Same McLachlan variational objective as the diffusion experiment.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Same boundary-condition handling as the diffusion experiment.

problem_instance.description: 2D diffusion/heat-equation benchmark used to study the effect of Monte Carlo batch size on runtime and accuracy.

dataset_specification.description: Fixed problem size examples with varying qubit-per-dimension settings; no external dataset.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Same synthetic Gaussian initialization and mesh discretization as the main diffusion experiment.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Runtime and average relative error versus forward Euler plotted against batch size.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: Problem-size dependent; figure labels indicate settings such as 3x4, 4x5, 5x5, 6x5 and 2x5, 3x4, 3x5, 4x4.

speedup_claims.caveats: Batch-size ablation studies accuracy/runtime tradeoff; no explicit classical speedup claim.

scalability_data.problem_size: fixed 2D diffusion problem, batch size varied
fixed 2D diffusion problem, batch size varied

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Runtime increases with batch size; overall algorithm remains polynomial in n as stated in the paper

experiments.description: Black-Scholes option-pricing experiment for 1D European call options, comparing the VMC-based solver against the analytic Black-Scholes formula and forward Euler across different volatilities, strikes, interest rates, and maturities.

algorithm.variant: Autoregressive neural-network quantum state solver for transformed Black-Scholes heat equation
algorithm.optimizer: Adam for pre-training; SVD-regularized linear update for evolution
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Pre-training and evolution run as in the diffusion experiment; evaluation at expiration time T
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Pre-trained to the transformed initial condition for each option-pricing setting

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The transformed heat-equation state is discretized on a mesh and represented as an n-qubit basis state.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve the transformed heat equation corresponding to the Black-Scholes PDE; option value recovered from the PDE solution.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Boundary values on the truncated domain are set using time-discounted payoff functions.

problem_instance.description: 1D European call option pricing under the Black-Scholes model.

dataset_specification.description: European call payoff Ψ(s)=max(s-K,0); compared against analytic Black-Scholes formula.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Black-Scholes PDE transformed to a heat equation using the Guillaume change of variables; domain truncated to [Ke^{-3σ√T}, Ke^{3σ√T}] and boundary values set by discounted payoff.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Option price at expiration compared to analytic ground truth and forward Euler; results reported in Figure 3 and Table 4.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: Not explicitly stated for the option-pricing runs; inherited from the mesh-based PDE discretization and varies with the chosen spatial grid.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Forward Euler and analytic Black-Scholes formula
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Transform Black-Scholes PDE to heat equation; truncate domain; impose discounted payoff boundary conditions.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Recover option price from transformed solution and compare relative error to analytic formula.

speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports accuracy comparisons only; no explicit speedup factor for option pricing.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Same polynomial-in-n VMC solver as the diffusion experiment

experiments.description: Black-Scholes option-pricing experiment for 2D basket call, basket put, rainbow max call, and spread put options, evaluated against forward Euler solutions.

algorithm.variant: Autoregressive neural-network quantum state solver for transformed multi-asset Black-Scholes heat equation
algorithm.optimizer: Adam for pre-training; SVD-regularized linear update for evolution
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Pre-trained to the transformed initial condition for each payoff

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 2D heat-equation state discretized on a mesh and encoded into an n-qubit basis state.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve the transformed 2D heat equation corresponding to the multi-asset Black-Scholes PDE.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Boundary conditions imposed using time-discounted payoff functions on the truncated hypercube domain.

problem_instance.description: Two-asset European option pricing under the Black-Scholes model for four payoff types: basket call, basket put, rainbow max call, and spread put.

dataset_specification.description: Payoffs listed in Table 3; no market dataset used.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Black-Scholes PDE transformed to heat equation; domain truncated to [Ke^{-3σ_i√T}, Ke^{3σ_i√T}]^d; boundary values set by discounted payoff.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Relative error of the VMC solution at expiration time versus forward Euler solution; reported in Table 4.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: Not explicitly stated for the 2D option-pricing runs; depends on the mesh discretization used for the transformed heat equation.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Transform Black-Scholes PDE to heat equation; truncate domain; impose discounted payoff boundary conditions.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare option prices at expiration time to Euler solution.

speedup_claims.caveats: Only relative errors are reported; no runtime or asymptotic speedup claim specific to this experiment.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Same polynomial-in-n VMC solver as the diffusion experiment

experiments.description: Dimensionality ablation for Black-Scholes basket-call pricing, showing option price versus strike for 1D, 2D, 3D, and 5D cases.

algorithm.optimizer: Adam for pre-training; SVD-regularized linear update for evolution

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Mesh-based encoding of the transformed heat-equation state into an n-qubit basis state.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve the transformed multi-asset Black-Scholes heat equation for basket-call pricing.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Truncated-domain boundary conditions via discounted payoff.

problem_instance.description: Basket European call option pricing as a function of dimensionality.

dataset_specification.description: Basket call payoff max(Σ w_i s_i - K, 0); dimensions shown are 1, 2, 3, and 5.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Black-Scholes-to-heat-equation transform; domain truncation and discounted payoff boundary conditions.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Option price versus strike K plotted for multiple dimensions.
